claims.text: The target material is bulk HfNbTaTiZr, both without oxygen addition and with 1 wt.% oxygen.
A machine-learning model should be trained using measurements from bulk HfNbTaTiZr with and without 1 wt.% oxygen.
Data-driven and computational tools are useful for exploring composition and temperature effects in high-entropy alloys.
Computational modeling of a high-entropy alloy can produce properties in quantitative agreement with first-principles calculations and experiments.
Training on measurements from oxygen-free and oxygen-containing specimens can improve prediction accuracy relative to existing analytical approaches.
The proposed accuracy improvement applies to conductivity predictions in the nearly 0–200 K regime.
The proposed accuracy improvement applies to conductivity predictions in the 300–1200 K regime.
The model can predict either thermal conductivity or electrical conductivity.
The model's advantage over existing analytical approaches is improved conductivity-prediction accuracy.
The model is limited to bulk HfNbTaTiZr with and without 1 wt.% oxygen.
The model is limited to the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature intervals.
Model performance depends on the quality and quantity of the training data.
Model performance depends on the selected machine-learning algorithm and hyperparameters.
The model should be benchmarked against experimental conductivity measurements in a held-out dataset.
The hypothesis is falsified if the model is not significantly more accurate than existing analytical approaches.
